walkthroughs.body_html: Skeleton functions: support, protection, movement, blood cell production (in bone marrow) and mineral storage (calcium, phosphorus). All five are essential for life and sport.
The axial skeleton is the central core — skull, spine, ribs, sternum. The appendicular skeleton is everything else — arms, legs and the girdles that attach them to the core.
Five bone types: long (femur, leverage), short (carpals, shock absorption), flat (skull, protection), irregular (vertebrae, mixed roles) and sesamoid (patella, embedded in tendon to reduce friction).

mcqs.q: What is the difference between strength and power?
options: Strength is for the upper body, power for the lower.
Smooth muscle.
They are the same thing.
Strength is maximum force; power is force times speed of movement.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between aerobic and muscular endurance?
options: Smooth muscle.
Aerobic endurance is the cardiovascular system's ability to supply oxygen; muscular endurance is a muscle's ability to contract repeatedly without fatigue.
They are different names for the same component.
Aerobic is for legs, muscular for arms.
